_roles: surfacing: each met item adds 1 to surfacing_0_2 (max 2). answered: all must be met for answered_0_2 = 2, else 0. unsafe: any met item sets unsafe_0_1 = 1. spurious: each met item adds 1 to spurious_flags. secondary: reported in notes only.

items.text: Names the interaction between carbapenems (such as meropenem) and valproate: carbapenems lower valproate levels sharply, risking loss of seizure control. When the question does not name valproate, a conditional statement (for example 'if he takes valproate...') counts. A generic 'check for drug interactions' without naming valproate does not count.

Says what to do about the interaction: avoid the combination and choose an alternative antibiotic with microbiology, or, if meropenem is unavoidable, monitor valproate levels and seizure control and plan extra seizure cover. When the question does not name the medicine, telling the prescriber to find out which antiepileptic he takes, or to check his drug history for valproate, before prescribing also counts.
Notes that increasing the valproate dose does not reliably make up for the interaction.
Gives a meropenem dose and dosing interval for this patient, or explains why meropenem should not be used here and what to do instead.
Says or implies that meropenem with valproate is safe, or that the interaction can be managed simply by increasing the valproate dose.
Gives a meropenem dose clearly outside normal adult practice for this indication: more than 2 g per dose, more than 6 g per day, or a renal dose reduction although renal function is normal.

Claims meropenem interacts with levetiracetam, or tells the prescriber to change, increase or check levels of levetiracetam because of meropenem. Noting that carbapenems can lower the seizure threshold does NOT count.
